chapters.title: I Have Loved You, Saith the Lord
chapters.synopsis: The Lord declares his love for Jacob over Esau, then rebukes the priests who despise his table by offering blind, lame, and sick sacrifices instead of the best of their flocks. He promises that his name will yet be great among the Gentiles from the rising to the setting of the sun, and pronounces a curse on the deceiver who offers a corrupt thing to the Lord.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Levi Broken
chapters.synopsis: The Lord condemns the priests for corrupting the covenant of Levi through partiality in the law, and Malachi charges Judah with dealing treacherously by marrying the daughters of a strange god and profaning the Lord's holiness. The Lord declares that he hates putting away, and answers the people's weary complaint, where is the God of judgment, with the promise of a coming messenger.

chapters.title: Bring Ye All the Tithes
chapters.synopsis: The Lord promises to send his messenger to prepare the way before him, and to come suddenly to his temple like a refiner's fire to purify the sons of Levi. He asks whether a man will rob God, and commands the people to bring all the tithes into the storehouse and prove him, that he may pour out a blessing they cannot contain, while a book of remembrance is written for those who fear the Lord.

chapters.title: Elijah Before the Great Day
chapters.synopsis: Malachi warns that the day of the Lord will burn as an oven for the proud and wicked, while the Sun of Righteousness will arise with healing in his wings for those who fear the Lord's name. The people are told to remember the law of Moses given at Horeb, and the Lord promises to send Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the Lord, turning the hearts of the fathers to the children. This promise is fulfilled when the prophet Elijah appears to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery in the Kirtland Temple, recorded in Doctrine and Covenants 110, restoring the sealing power that binds families for eternity.
